newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Nearly half of Palestinians back suicide bombs.
newsitem.headline: Nearly half of Palestinians back suicide bombs.

text.p: Nearly half of all Palestinians in an opinion poll support suicide attacks against Israel as support for peace talks with the Jewish state plummets, a Palestinian research centre said on Sunday.

Dr Nabil Kukali, president of the Palestinian Centre for Public Opinion (PCPO) near Bethlehem, said 48.6 of Palestinians surveyed supported suicide bombings such as an attack last month that killed three Israeli women at a Tel Aviv cafe.
The survey of 470 Palestinians from Jerusalem, Bethlehem and Hebron said only 37.5 percent opposed suicide attacks.
"I feel the Palestinian people are getting more radical concerning suicide attacks in Israel," Kukali told Reuters.

Israeli-PLO peace talks plunged into crisis last month when Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu began construction of a new Jewish settlement in Arab East Jerusalem, claimed by both Israel and the PLO.

Three Palestinians have been killed by Israeli soldiers and scores wounded in unrest sparked by the settlement plan. In addition to the Tel Aviv cafe bombing, two Islamic Jihad militants blew themselves up last week in a pair of botched suicide attacks in Gaza.
Kukali said 37.2 percent of Palestinians polled between March 26-31 favoured severing peace talks with Israel and 19.2 percent wanted them to continue but with new negotiators.
"There is now a gap between the Palestinian people and the Palestinian Authority, especially to the people who negotiate with Israel. The majority of Palestinians don't trust them."

The PCPO poll said that 62.9 percent of those polled rated the Palestinian Authority's handling of peace talks as "below average" or a "failure". Kukali said 95.9 percent held Netanyahu responsible for the present impasse.
The poll had a margin of error of 3.5 percent.
